properties.decision:
SETTLED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-16: DO IT, BUT NOT YET. His ruling: "I'd like to actually define 'black boxes' and define contracts between them - this is not immediate (priority is resolving bugs)".

⇒ OPTIONS (b) AND (c) ARE CHOSEN — declare the internal seams, and declare the foundation layer that the cohesion verdict currently rests on. Option (a) do-nothing is REJECTED; (d) subsystem-level allocation bookkeeping and (e) do-it-in-public were not taken up.
⇒ SEQUENCING IS PART OF THE RULING, not a note beside it: BUG WORK FIRST. `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating` and its five requirements come before this.

⭐ HIS STATED REASON FOR ACCEPTING THE DELAY, and it is the answer to the question that opened this whole thread: "this conversation has led me to believe reflow2, when used on other projects, will actually lead you through a principled SE process (therefore the delay in properly modularizing reflow2 itself)."

⇒ THE SELF-HOST GAP IS NO LONGER READ AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE PRODUCT. That is what makes the deferral defensible rather than merely convenient: the reason to hurry would have been that reflow2's own state implied something about what it does for its users, and the guided paths were found to sequence function before structure independently of the self-host. `genesis` seeds P0/P1 and STOPS before Components; `adopt` forbids inferring a Requirement from the implementation that satisfies it.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND UNCHANGED BY THE DEFERRAL, so nobody later mistakes "deferred" for "resolved":
• 73 coupled module pairs, ZERO sharing a declared Interface, 51 crossing a subsystem boundary. All 15 Interfaces sit at the SYSTEM edge; none describes an internal boundary.
• The swap test: `cmp:detect` — 13 functions, 2 dependents, ZERO declared interfaces. Same for every module measured. There is nothing to swap against.
• reflow2's own graph still does not do what its own `adopt` skill tells every user to do: "both sides of every contract".
• The eight subsystems ARE a deliberate functional carving (`dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`, accepted 2026-07-23, derived with the user) and they ARE cohesive — six couplings cross peer subsystems against 17 inside. The boxes are real; only the contracts are missing.
⚠️ And that cohesion verdict rests on treating Store and Vocabulary as FOUNDATION, which is an ASSUMPTION A READER SUPPLIES rather than something the design declares — which is why option (c), declaring the layer, is part of what was chosen rather than an afterthought.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it sets the cost when this is picked up: how many distinct CONTRACTS the 51 crossing pairs collapse into. The figure counts PAIRS and the real number is likely far smaller. Measuring that first would size the work before committing to it.
properties.name: Define reflow2's black boxes and the contracts between them — DEFERRED behind bug work, on Anthony's word
properties.rationale: Anthony's ruling, 2026-08-16, given at the close of the systems-engineering thread he opened the same day. The measurements are mine; the choice, the priority ordering, and the reason for accepting the delay are his. Recorded as ACCEPTED with the work deferred rather than left `proposed`, because a deferral IS a decision — leaving it open would misreport an answered question as an unanswered one, and `arrival_delta` would keep asking. The sibling `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` stays `proposed`: he stated a BELIEF about it, not a ruling, and the distinction is his to close.
